clue.text: Comedy team is evergreen and resilient

parts.note: the laurel is an evergreen shrub
taken as written
hardy means tough and able to endure

explanation.surface: A description of a comedy double act as long-lasting and tough.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as two adjectives praising a team; each is really a word in the duo's names.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy were the famous slapstick double act of early Hollywood film.

clue.text: Fear Capone with a weapon

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, supplies his first name
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: Being afraid of a gangster who is armed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden anxiety or apprehension, a synonym for fear.

clue.text: Reluctantly to begin with, I pardon lousy bit of weather

indicators.note: tells us to take only the opening letter of reluctantly

parts.note: supplies its first letter

indicators.note: something lousy is in poor shape, so these letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly granting forgiveness during a spell of bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of rain is a small piece of the weather.

clue.text: Sanctioned part of a trip with Muhammad, ending in London

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a journey
Muhammad Ali, the boxer
the alphabet's last letter is called zed by Londoners, rather than zee

explanation.surface: A permitted stretch of a journey taken alongside a famous boxer, finishing in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Americanised -IZE spelling ends in Z, which a British speaker names ZED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise it, so a sanctioned act has been made lawful.

clue.text: Former Indian leader exalting primordial chicken?

indicators.note: exalting means lifting up, and in a down entry lifting reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: the prefix ur- means primitive or original, as in Urtext
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: An Indian statesman glorifying the first chicken, as in which came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister after independence.

clue.text: Bob, for one, is rigorous about intelligence operations up front

indicators.note: the word for rigorous goes around the intelligence letter

parts.note: hard can mean demanding and strict
I is short for intelligence

indicators.note: only the front letter of operations is used

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A man named Bob is strict about spy work that is done openly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name; it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, one example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Encore "Repeat something on a list, nearly at speed (7)" for anyone who solved last week's puzzle

definitions.text: Encore "Repeat something on a list, nearly at speed (7)" for anyone who solved last week's puzzle

parts.note: encore means again, which is the prefix re-

parts.words: Repeat something on a list, nearly at speed (7)
parts.note: last week's clue, solved by ITEM nearly (ITE) plus RATE for speed, defined by repeat

explanation.surface: The setters run last week's clue again for solvers who remember it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted clue gave a seven-letter answer last week; putting 'again' in front of it builds this week's answer, and the clue is itself a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something again, as this clue does with last week's, is to reiterate it.

clue.text: Americans can be jerks

explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to insult Americans; jerks is a verb meaning sharp pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a nickname for people from the United States and a verb for tugging sharply.

clue.text: Altering integral for mathematical figure

indicators.note: altering a word changes it, so the letters of integral are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken just as written in the clue

explanation.surface: Changing an integral to produce a figure in a maths problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided polygon, a basic shape of geometry.

clue.text: Railroad that is one of the three R's

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... Railroad, a Pennsylvania line famous from Monopoly
second meaning: ..., writing and arithmetic are the basic school skills

explanation.walkthrough: The R of Railroad hints at the three R's; the Reading line is pronounced 'redding' but spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling names a historic American rail company and the first of the basic skills taught in school.

clue.text: McKellen follows head-over-heels Thai island resident

indicators.note: the actor's name comes after the other piece
the head letter of Thai tumbles to the far end, past the heels

parts.note: taken as written, then its first letter is shifted to the end
Ian McKellen, the British actor

explanation.surface: The actor Ian McKellen comes after a Thai islander who is madly in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Head-over-heels reads as smitten, but it moves the first letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Haiti, the nation sharing Hispaniola in the Caribbean, lives on an island.

clue.text: Directed and edited media

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so the letters of media are reordered

parts.note: anagram fodder taken just as written in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone who ran and edited news outlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimed and directed both mean pointed or steered toward a target.

clue.text: She washes, as the Spanish disrobe

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in Spanish
to disrobe is to take one's clothes off

explanation.surface: A woman doing the washing, undressing the way Spaniards do.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash clothes and linen.

clue.text: Ugly female novelist makes cheese

parts.note: a gorgon is a hideous woman, after Medusa and her sisters
Emile Zola, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A plain woman who writes novels makes cheese on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue-veined cheese.

clue.text: Complex procedure to equip Gertrude or Jocasta, for example

parts.note: to rig is to fit out, as with a ship
both are stage mothers, Hamlet's and Oedipus's, so each is a ma role

explanation.surface: A plan to supply two tragic queens, as if for a production.
explanation.walkthrough: Complex points at the Oedipus complex, and Jocasta is Oedipus's mother; in fact it starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious and complicated process.

clue.text: Country inhabited by sleepy yes-men?

parts.note: the drowsy realm of sleep in the old phrase
yes-men agree by nodding their heads, a second kind of nodding

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for sleep, from the biblical place east of Eden, also suits a nation of people who nod yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the state of being asleep is a place where everyone nods, whether drowsing or agreeing.

clue.text: Soft melody for two

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A gentle tune arranged as a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a couple or duo is a set of exactly two matching items or people.

clue.text: Hold back to filter again?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., to strain once more

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is a pun built from re- and strain.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to keep under control, and split up it suggests passing liquid through a sieve a second time.

clue.text: Carol, about long-running TV show: "It's first-rate"

indicators.note: the word for carol goes around the show's name

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
M*A*S*H, the US sitcom about army medics that ran for eleven seasons

explanation.surface: Someone singing about a classic TV series and praising it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal praise meaning excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Border divided Germany down the middle

indicators.note: the answer straddles the split between the two words, running down their middle

parts.note: the letters run from the end of divided into the start of Germany

explanation.surface: The frontier that cut postwar Germany in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the inner German border; the letters sit across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a boundary or rim, a synonym for border.

clue.text: Unusual pain killers: they are used in The Three Musketeers and The Seven Samurai

definitions.text: they are used in The Three Musketeers and The Seven Samurai

parts.note: odd means strange
read as numb-ers, things that numb pain

explanation.surface: Strange painkillers, then a remark about two classic adventure stories.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBERS splits as numb-ers, things that deaden pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Three and seven, in the two titles, are integers not divisible by two.

clue.text: In Chad, Rupert reversed seclusion

indicators.note: those letters are then read in the opposite direction
the letters are found inside the words Chad and Rupert

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of Chad and the start of Rupert

explanation.surface: A man called Rupert retreating from the world in the African country of Chad.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the practice of keeping women secluded from public view, so it means seclusion.

clue.text: Locals finally outsquat stranger where things are now

indicators.note: stranger means more peculiar, so the letters are jumbled
only the final letter of locals is used

parts.note: supplies its last letter
anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Residents are pushed out by an incomer who squats better than they do.
explanation.definitionFit: The status quo is the existing state of affairs.

clue.text: Look what I did: at first, successfully resurrected slain Arab leader

indicators.note: raised up, which in a down entry reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: ta-da is the cry of someone revealing a trick

indicators.note: only the first letter of successfully is used

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A conjurer boasts of bringing a dead leader back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat, Egypt's president, was assassinated in 1981.

clue.text: Letters in marquee reveal title of William Burroughs opus

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters sitting inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run from inside marquee into the start of reveal

explanation.surface: A theater sign announcing the name of a Burroughs work.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer is William S. Burroughs's short novel, written in the 1950s and published in 1985.

clue.text: Stray wantonly with lecher

indicators.note: acting wantonly means acting without restraint, so the letters run loose

parts.note: anagram fodder taken just as written in the clue

explanation.surface: A womaniser who wanders off to misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: Stray looks like the definition; it is the fodder, and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr, the lustful woodland god of Greek myth, is used for a lustful man.

clue.text: Endeavored to overlook source for valuable collection

indicators.note: the source is the opening letter, which is ignored

parts.note: strove means tried hard

explanation.surface: Someone tried to ignore where a treasure came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuable things, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Determined opening game piece

parts.note: a door is an opening in a wall
a die is a cube thrown in board games

explanation.surface: A resolute first move with a game counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-or-die describes an all-out effort, a resolve to succeed whatever it takes.

clue.text: Rani ruined belt in African city

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of rani are broken up

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written; a rani is an Indian queen
an obi is a Japanese sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: An Indian queen's sash spoilt while she visits an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: Strenuous questioning for a PhD, often

definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving someone ... is grilling them hard
second meaning: a doctorate usually follows a bachelor's and a master's, making it one's third degree

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the idiom literally: a doctorate comes after two earlier degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for harsh interrogation also counts the academic qualifications a doctor of philosophy collects.
